free_tier.stated: No byte quota — a $400 credit balance and a 30-day clock, whichever ends first. 'The trial continues for 30 days (from the sign-up date) or until you've depleted your free usage balance.' Storage accrues cost against that balance at standard rates (~$40/TB/month per the documented Standard rate). So the nominal free storage is whatever the credit buys after compute: at $40/TB/mo, $400 buys 10 TB-months, i.e. 10 TB for one month or 1 TB for ten.

egress.terms: Not free. Snowflake bills egress/transfer separately and the trial credit is consumed by it.

tooling: Excellent: PUT to an internal stage, full SQL, Snowflake SDKs, and external stages pointing at your own S3/Azure/GCS. Programmatically the best of the warehouse entrants.
chaining: One trial per email; trials cannot be chained legitimately because the account is suspended at day 30 — 'At the end of the trial, the account is suspended. You can still log into a suspended account, but you cannot use any features, such as … loading data.'
limits_note: retention-clamped and hard-capped by design. Data is NOT deleted on suspension but is also not retrievable, which is worse than deletion for the purpose of treating it as storage. Identity is email only, which is the one thing in its favour.
reliability_note: Suspension at day 30 makes this a 30-day buffer, not storage. Any chunked-object scheme built on it would need a full re-upload cycle monthly.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

surfaced: '200 free credits, a $400 value' — the credit figure, confirming the balance framing.
surfaced: '$40/TB/month in storage' on standard plan, which is the rate the credit is spent against.
